thread:
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Canary deployment `text-gen/web-v2` in us-west-2 breaching abort criteria. 5xx rate at 18% over last 2m (threshold 10%). Canary ID: canary-78a3. Routing: 5% of traffic. Paging on-call. Dashboard: https://infra.redwood.ai/mon/rollouts/canary-78a3
Mira: Oncall Mira here, grabbing it. Which deployment config is this?
Samir: That’s the autoprobing rollout from git commit abc1234 -> web-model:v2. I can start mitigation.
Jen: Seeing repeated OOMs in model-worker logs for canary tasks with seq_len ~2048. Stack shows `cudaMemcpy` failures then 5xx.
Paul: I’m on logs/dashboard, confirming 5xx cluster-wide localized to canary nodes. Stable pool healthy.
Mira: OK. Abort criteria hit (5xx>10%). Plan: 1) remove traffic from canary, 2) flip feature flag `use_web_v2` to false, 3) trigger revert deploy if needed. Who’s doing which?
Samir: I’ll remove traffic first — can do a traffic split change to 0% for canary and enable kill-switch flag. Command I’ll run:
```
# trafficctl set-split --canary canary-78a3 --percent 0
curl -XPOST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $SRE_TOKEN' https://flags.redwood.ai/flags/use_web_v2 -d '{"value":false}'
```
Samir: running now.
Ops Bot: Action acknowledged: trafficctl request accepted. Canary canary-78a3 -> 0% (in progress).
Samir: traffic now 0% (confirmed by routing logs).
Paul: Good. I’m seeing canary instances terminate their active KV cache. No incoming inference requests.
Jen: Feature flag flip succeeded. `use_web_v2=false` across regions.
Mira: Great — confirm rollback plan? Do we want an immediate revert of the deployment artifact or just keep canary disabled and troubleshoot?
Samir: Given OOMs at seq len 2048, probably model binary needs a fix (memory pool sizing). Revert to previous stable model on canary nodes to be safe. I’ll kick a revert job: `deployctl revert --service web --to stable~2026-03-14`
Ops Bot: Revert job queued: job-id 2026031501. Estimated time ~3m.
Jen: I’ve captured a minimal reproducer and pushed logs to the incident bucket: gs://redwood-incidents/1759002468/logs.txt — includes stack snippet: `RuntimeError: cuMemAlloc failed`.
Mira: Any customer-visible errors? Pager shows only internal alerting. No support tickets yet.
Paul: Quick check against request logs: no 5xx surge from customer-facing endpoints; the canary route header shows traffic was only 5% and has been drained. No known customer impact.
Samir: Revert finished. Canary host set back to stable model. Running healthchecks.
Ops Bot: Healthchecks: canary group -> OK (3/3 checks pass). 5xx rate for canary group dropped to 0.8%.
Mira: Nice. Marking incident as mitigated. Postmortem actions: - Jen to root cause (model memory) and PR with fix + canary test for long seqs. - Samir to add autoscaler guard for mem pressure. - Paul to draft customer note if anything surfaces.
Jen: Adding checklist: add a synthetic with seq_len=2048 to canary smoke tests, and run quantized memory profiling. Will create PR and link here.
Samir: Also adding a safety net: abort on OOM logs in canary should trigger immediate traffic drain. I’ll add an alert rule.
Mira: Thanks team. Handoff: I’m oncall for another 2 hours; if anything regresses page oncall-next. Labeling thread: incident:canary-abort-1759002468 (internal only).
Paul: :white_check_mark: closing loop. I’ll watch dashboards for 15m then archive incident.
Jen: Will follow up with RCA doc and timeline.
Incident Bot: Incident mitigated by actions from Samir and Ops Bot. Monitoring for 30m.
Mira: End of thread — thanks all for quick response. :thumbsup:
